The scatter plot above gives the correspondence between the variables $x$ and $y$ for some data points. Estimate the value of $y$ when $x=23.$ 

*Hint: Assume the trend is linear, and that the trend line passes through the points $(11,8)$ and $(15,7).$*
question.worked_solution:
First, using the hint, let's draw an approximate trend line for our scatter plot.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14227574/assets/b9dbed9bab9d769f7408006854bd0c159cb980bfa5f4441fe1b4e5753dfbc078.png)

Our trend line passes through $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(11,8)$ and $({x}_{2},{y}_{2})=(15,7).$

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form 

$$
y=mx+b.
$$

First, we calculate the slope $m$ of the line as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{7-8}{15-11} \\  & =\frac{(-1)}{4} \\  & =-0.25\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $m=-0.25$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y=-0.25x+b.
$$

We now need to calculate the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can do this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(11,8):$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-0.25x+b \\ 8 & =-0.25(11)+b \\ 8 & =-2.75+b \\ b & =10.75\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=-0.25x+10.75.
$$

Finally, we substitute $x=23$ into the equation above, which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-0.25x+10.75 \\  & =-0.25(23)+10.75 \\  & =-5.75+10.75 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, according to this model, when $x=23$ we have $y≈5.$

Note: The point where $x=23$ is not shown on our trend line. Therefore, our result *may* be unreliable.
